title: Phu Quoc food: 5 dishes to try
region: Đặc khu Phú Quốc, An Giang, Việt Nam

scenes.narration: What to eat in Phu Quoc? Here are five dishes you have to try, with where they come from, how they are made, how to eat them, and places checked on Google Maps. Flip each card with me!
scenes.label: REGIONAL FOOD
scenes.caption: PHU QUOC

scenes.narration: Dish one, herring salad. According to VnExpress, islanders once made salads from many kinds of fish after a trip at sea, and over time chose herring as the best. Very fresh herring is cut into two fillets, mixed with a sour dressing, then topped with herbs, shallots, chili and grated coconut. To eat, roll the fish in rice paper with wild greens and herbs, and dip it in Phu Quoc fish sauce with peanuts. Try the Lobster Cave, Dao Hai San, or Phuong Hoang.
scenes.caption: Gỏi cá trích

scenes.narration: Dish two, bun quay, or stirred noodles. Its origin has several versions: some say it came to the island from central Vietnam, others that the Kien Xay shop near Dinh Cau made it famous. Fresh noodles are pressed on the spot, covered in broth, with shrimp paste and fish balls. It is called stirred noodles because to eat, you stir your own dipping sauce of sugar, kumquat, chili and fish sauce to taste. Try Bach Dang, Thien My, or Co Tham.

scenes.narration: Dish three, grilled sea urchin with scallion oil. Nhum is the local name for sea urchin, gathered fresh around the island. Each one is cut in half, drizzled with scallion oil and grilled over charcoal, then topped with fried shallots and roasted peanuts. To eat, spoon out the rich, creamy meat; some places also make sea urchin porridge. Tip: ask whether it is sea urchin or murex snail, since some menus mix them up. Try Hau Nuong Nhum Nuong eight K, or Thuan Kieu.

scenes.narration: Dish four is seafood you pick live from the tank. Phu Quoc has many fishing villages, and the most famous catch is Ham Ninh crab from the east coast, caught close to shore, so the meat is firm, sweet and full of roe. At the night market and seafood restaurants, you choose a live one from the tank, it is weighed, and the kitchen boils, steams or grills it. To eat, crab with salt, pepper and lime is all you need. Tip: ask the price per kilo and the cooking fee first. Try MYLA, Su and Bee seafood, or KTIN.
scenes.caption: Hải sản chọn tại bể

scenes.narration: Number five is the one to take home, Phu Quoc fish sauce. Fish sauce making in Phu Quoc is recognised as national intangible cultural heritage. Fresh anchovies are layered with salt in big wooden vats for twelve to eighteen months before the first sauce is drawn off. To eat, use it as the dip for fish salad, noodle soup and seafood. Buy it at the Huynh Khoa or Thanh Khoa fish sauce houses, or the Khai Hoan specialty centre.
